newsitem.title: FRANCE: Air France hopes for profit advance, privatisation.
newsitem.headline: Air France hopes for profit advance, privatisation.

text.p: State carrier Air France, which announced a return to a small profit on Thursday, said it hoped to improve on the result in the current year and renewed its argument that privatisation made economic sense.

Bolstered by a net consolidated profit of 394 million francs in the year to end-March, the first profit since 1989, managing director Patrice Durand said he hoped Air France would be "a bit more than at breakeven" at the end of a year in which it will absorb its short- and medium-haul subsidiary in a merger.

He argued strongly for privatisation, which has been slated by the centre-right government. The government is fighting a two-round parliamentary election runoff on Sunday after losing to the left wing parties in the first round.
"We are a public enterprise but one which lives in a totally competitive world just like goods and services companies. Economic logic weighs heavily in favour of privatisation."

"The return to breakeven shows Air France has the ability to capitalise on its qualities. We believe that if we don't make too many errors we could be up there close to British Airways in a few years," Durand told reporters.
